title: Greek Magical Papyri Tradition — Practical Magic Texts from Egypt
description: The Greek Magical Papyri (Papyri Graecae Magicae, PGM) represent a corpus of practical magic handbooks from Greco-Roman Egypt dated primarily to the 2nd-4th centuries CE, preserved in the dry Egyptian climate. These texts contain instructions for love spells, curse tablets, healing rituals, divination, and spirit invocation, mixing Greek, Egyptian, Jewish, and Christian elements in a syncretic tradition. They demonstrate that organized magical practice with written textual traditions existed well below the level of philosophical or literary magic, among practitioners serving everyday client needs. The PGM are foundational evidence for Hans Dieter Betz, John Gager, and other scholars reconstructing ancient magic practice.
historiographical_note: Hans Dieter Betz's 1986 edition of the Greek Magical Papyri in Translation fundamentally transformed scholarship on ancient magic, demonstrating the gap between elite literary representations of magic and actual practitioner texts.
source_method: Published scholarship; Betz (ed.) Greek Magical Papyri in Translation (1986); Gager, Curse Tablets
